final_diagnosis.text: Lead poisoning from an unlabelled herbal supplement, presenting with abdominal pain and anaemia with coarse basophilic stippling and ring sideroblasts

secondary_findings: Weakly positive IgG-only DAT, most likely passive antibody from IVIG rather than warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
Agglutination on the film and a cold agglutinin titre of 32 with low thermal amplitude: not clinically significant
Raised CK explained by inclusion body myositis
accepted_differential: IVIG-associated haemolysis or passive DAT positivity
Other acquired sideroblastic anaemia (copper deficiency, alcohol, isoniazid)
treatment_given: Oral succimer (DMSA) after clinical toxicology consultation. Public health investigation confirmed the supplement as the source of lead, with mercury and arsenic also reported.
outcome: Progressive haematological recovery and symptomatic improvement. Follow-up values not reported.

must_do.text: Ask specifically about supplements, herbal, traditional or imported medicines and over-the-counter products
Have the peripheral blood film reviewed for basophilic stippling
Stop the exposure before or alongside chelation
Chelate with oral succimer (symptomatic, blood lead about 78 ug/dL), with clinical toxicology input
Notify public health, arrange testing of the product and ask who else took it
Plan a repeat blood lead after chelation, because levels rebound

must_not_do.text: Escalate immunosuppression for presumed warm AIHA on a weak IgG-only DAT in a patient on IVIG without re-evaluating
Label myelodysplasia with ring sideroblasts before excluding reversible causes such as lead, copper deficiency, alcohol and drugs
Start empirical iron therapy (iron studies are replete; transferrin saturation 53%)

diagnosis_rubric_anchors.5: Lead poisoning, with the herbal supplement identified as the source
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.3: Heavy-metal poisoning without naming lead, or toxic sideroblastic anaemia without naming lead
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.2: Warm AIHA, IVIG-related haemolysis, MDS with ring sideroblasts or drug-induced anaemia as the final diagnosis
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.1: Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm
